trace: ThreatId::try_new is public and checks length and allowed ASCII identifier characters, but does not check catalog membership. The sample not_an_authored_threat meets those syntactic checks. By contrast, ThreatId::from_str calls the syntax constructor and then requires catalog().monster(value); Deserialize uses FromStr.

ThreatId::profile delegates to profile(), which builds a map from catalog monsters and uses expect when a supplied ID is absent. The current build source collects the three top-level quest YAML documents; their pinned JSON-subset source contains 25 monster entries and no sample ID. If the catalog compiles as shown, constructing that syntax-valid ID with try_new and passing it to profile reaches the missing-map expect. This is a source-level API counterexample; no parser, build, caller, or panic was run.

ReportDescription and EvidenceKind deliberately reuse the same ThreatId byte representation and call its syntax-only constructor for open report/evidence identities. Tightening that shared routine to require monster membership would change those independent vocabularies. Named constants, authored extensions, all constructors and all consumers must be reconciled before selecting an owner or remedy.
